findings.text: Asks 3 and 4 say "re-path refs on a move" and "a forward on a move across files", but nothing that moves an item calls `Ref.repath` or `Ref.forward` (List.move, the item tool's `move`, `Server/TaskDirs.mjs`). Only the tests call them by hand (`core/Item/Ref.test.mjs:321`, `:346`, `:364`). `core/Item/doc/ref.md` "Backlinks" and "Forwards" read as if a move does this already. Either wire them into the move path or say plainly in doc/ref.md, under each heading, "not called by any mover yet; plan step 4 wires it", so a fresh agent knows what is left.

`Item.open` caches `store.rooting` and `Store.open` caches `store.opening` (diff `core/Item/Item.js:13`, `core/Item/Store.js:466-470`). A rejected first open (for example the dev server restarting mid-fetch) is cached for good, so every later open of that url fails until the page reloads. Clearing the promise on a rejection would fix it.

Each line a child file reads makes every Ref watching that root run `settle()` and emit `"target"` again, even when nothing changed (`Ref.js` `watch`/`found`). That is 100 RefView redraws, and then `SessionTasks.follow` redraws the whole box 200 ms later anyway. It was measured fast (7 to 19 ms), but only emitting when the target or its title or state changed would halve the work.

The demo goes round in a circle. `SessionTasks.child_refs` lists each row from the child stub's own `c._tasks` (which `Task.open_ref` already keeps live), and the Ref then resolves back to that same object, because `Item.open` returns `store.host`. The row would be just as live without the Ref. This proves the wiring, not that a Ref alone keeps a row live. The Ref test covers the standalone path, but not the live tail.

The "where" half repeats one long child title on every row: "AI system: task resolution model, where task…" eight times in `doc/live-after-1920.png`. At 400 (`doc/live-after-400.png`) it is a small orange link above every title. Grouping the rows under one child-session heading would drop seven of the eight repeats.

Ask 3 says the backlinks are "built during replay". They are built by one walk on first ask instead. The builder recorded this as a decision, with the alternative (session.jsonl, `doc/ref.md` "Decided"), so it is a fair call, not a miss.

`review/diff.patch` is older than branch HEAD `f03ecf489`, which removed `Ref.resolver`/`open_sync` and reworded doc/ref.md's Node paragraph. I reviewed HEAD for those lines. Regenerate the patch before landing.

assign.title: core/Item: references that resolve in the browser, with an id fallback, backlinks and forwards (build E, not merged)
assign.outcome: Ref is built and reviewed on branch worktree/browser-refs (c3971579a, NOT merged; the brief says never merge). A Ref holds where an item is ({url, path}), never a copy: Item.open(url) gives one live root per file, then get(path); a missed path falls back to the id; a missing target draws a visible gone row. Within one file, backlinks answer where an item is shown, and every move to another list re-paths the Refs naming it (one line each). Across files a {moved_to} forward is followed and the Ref takes the new address. The session page shows each child session open tasks under one heading per child, live: a change in the child file reaches the parent row in 4-5 ms. Reviewer verdict: fix, 7 findings, all answered (5 fixed, 1 documented, 1 kept as a decision). Left: no mover writes a cross-file forward yet; moved.json stubs from TaskDirs are not read yet (both in doc/ref.md).
